title: OpenWarrant Format 1.0: checklist item
description: Hand-written and normative for docs/format/FORMAT-1.0.md section 3.8 and Appendix A `item`. Where this schema and the prose disagree, the prose wins and this schema is the defect. One item line `- [ ] <text> (<item-id>[, after <ref>]…)[ — done by <actor>, <YYYY-MM-DD>[: <note>]]` as a reader holds it: `done` is the box (`[x]` and `[X]` are done, `[ ]` open), `after` each `after` reference in order, and `done_by`, `done_on`, `level` and `note` the optional completion; `level` is draft 3's tick level (` [observed]`, ` [independent]` or ` [signed]`, section 11.4; `claimed` writes none). `implements <id>` in the text is a relation (section 3.8), listed in `implements`. A box line with no id group is reported (`format.item-id-missing`) and has no `id`; a writer assigns one. Boxes other than `[ ]`, `[x]` and `[X]` are refused (`format.item`) and never reach this shape.

after.description: Appendix A `item-ref`: an item, a ticket, or another ticket's item.

done_by.description: The actor that ticked the box.

allOf.description: Appendix A `done`: only a done item carries a completion.
Appendix A `done`: `done by <actor>, <date>` come together, and a note follows them.
Appendix A `item`: an `after` reference sits in the id group, so an item without an id has none.
